A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same scaling-law study and QueCC compression method despite the changed title. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 3–4 report original scaling experiments, validation on 14B models, and QueCC benchmark results. Appendix A.3 includes additional scaling-law validation plots.

after.justification: The original empirical results remain, supplemented by PruMerge scaling experiments, a zero-visual-token control, and component ablations in Appendix A.4.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same QueCC procedure: query-embedding injection, depth-wise convolutional downsampling, local cross-attention, and an MLP. The revised compressor description for the scaling experiments concerns their reported setup; it does not establish a redesign of QueCC.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine-benchmark scaling suite, DocVQA/TextVQA OCR evaluations, and eight QueCC benchmarks. The new experiments vary compressors and model components on retained tasks rather than adding datasets or application domains.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds a No Visual Tokens comparator, and new Table 3 compares against LLaMA-VID, previously only cited. PruMerge also enters the scaling-law validation in Section 3.5, having previously participated only in the compression-method benchmark comparison.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 revises the stated scaling-study compressor from TokenPacker to a convolutional variant without query injection; this does not establish that experiments were rerun. New Section 3.5 evaluates PruMerge with 0.5B, 1.8B, and 4B models and 36–576 visual tokens, comparing fixed versus refitted scaling constants. Zero-vision and factorial component-removal controls substantially extend the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v2 adds cross-compressor generalization tests in Section 3.5, a zero-visual-token control, and four-way convolution/query ablations at 1, 4, and 16 tokens in Appendix A.4. These directly test generality and component contributions. The earlier query-length, OCR, token-repetition, and 14B extrapolation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The retained less-than-2% extrapolation error describes prediction accuracy, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: The original Table 1 scores and scaling plots are unchanged. v2 adds PruMerge fits with alpha/beta values of 0.069/0.008 when constants are fixed and 0.077/0.041 when refitted, plus zero-token, component-ablation, and LLaMA-VID results. Section 4.2 corrects the reported one-token gap comparisons. New Table 2 also lists one-token QueCC TextVQA as 46.9, conflicting with 46.8 in both versions' Table 1.

T1.justification: Equation 2 is unchanged, but Section 3.1 changes the stated definition of T from visual input tokens to total inference tokens. Subsequent explanations and the fitting grid still treat T as visual-token count, making this a limited, internally inconsistent definition revision. No new proofs or theorems appear.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that inference-optimal visual reasoning favors larger LLMs with very few visual tokens, sometimes one for cached queries, and propose query-conditioned compression. The OCR exception remains. The broader title reflects qualifications already present in v1, while the new experiments support an already asserted cross-compressor generalization claim.

C2.justification: Section 3.5 newly attributes PruMerge's extreme-compression failures to its training-free design. Appendix A.4 interprets query injection and convolution as complementary components that can mitigate individual performance drops. v2 also explicitly ties the fivefold exponent comparison to the selected Qwen family and compressor; existing OCR and long-query qualifications remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the convolutional, query-free TokenPacker variant used for scaling and documents the new PruMerge fitting configurations. Appendix A.4 identifies LLaMA-VID's additional context token and separate text decoder. The code URL, inherited training-setup references, and Appendix A.2 grid-search ranges remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged. Appendix A.4 adds substantive positioning against LLaMA-VID, acknowledging its stronger vision encoder and distinguishing its separate text decoder from QueCC's reuse of the existing LLM. The central positioning around joint optimization under an inference budget remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of Section 3.3 are rewritten or condensed to foreground fewer tokens and more parameters and reorganize the cached versus variable-query discussion. The token-repetition discussion moves, OCR becomes Section 3.4, Section 4 is retitled, and the appendix gains a dedicated ablation subsection.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel PruMerge Figure 5, appendix Tables 2–3, and a zero-token row in Table 1. Existing plot graphics and the QueCC schematic are retained, with caption edits, renumbering, relocation, and modest layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The new compressor-generalization checks and component ablations strengthen support for the retained conclusions. The zero-token control, LLaMA-VID comparison, and corrected Section 4.2 gap claims also improve evaluation and reporting. These gains are tempered by PruMerge validation excluding the 1–16-token regime and newly introduced inconsistencies in the definition of T and the one-token TextVQA value. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net improvement.
